$comment: Performance budgets. Baselines are first measurements; a check fails when a value regresses past its section's allowedRegression, and a section without a baseline is reported, not failed. openingFrameTime: just perf-opening (record with: just perf-opening record), headless Chromium since #48 (ADR 0144): its frames come on a 60 Hz clock, so p50 and p95 read 16.7 ms while the onboarding frame keeps up, against WebKit's 17 and 18. startup, idleMemory, inputLatency, freshDeskAtRest, deskOutOfSight, residentAtRest: just perf-app on the CEF desk, nightly in the e2e workflow's perf job; their baselines come from the CI runner (just perf-app record, or budgets.json from the job's artifact), and none was recorded on the Tauri app, so the CEF desk's first run sets them. targetMs are RT-16's targets, printed beside the values, not gates. compose, composeStartup, surfaceStartup, surfaceMemory, inputToPaint, inputFromRest, deskAtRest: just perf-compositor (#58, e2e/perf/lib/compositor.ts) on the reference machine (docs/qa/TESTING.md); each section says why in its reason. budgetMs is a budget the value stays under, allowedRegression an allowance past a baseline, band a share either side of one; a baseline recorded on another platform or with another tool, and a budget on a software adapter, are reported, never failed.

startup.reason: #370 (ADR 0261): a second start with a saved session of six surfaces, through just perf-app's start-up spec (e2e/perf/startup.perf.ts), the median of two runs' medians of three relaunches each on the reference machine on 2026-11-21, a debug bundle of main a6a50ba9 with chromedriver attached, started at a load average of 4.2 and 9.5 with other sessions building: readyMs 1838.5 and 1840.4, firstFrameMs 1851.1 and 1860.8. All six opens answered and every relaunch's trace had the six mount phases; no GPU process exited. A third run at a load of 6.8 read 1993.1 and 2008.4. Fails past allowedRegression on the platform its baseline was recorded on.

idleMemory.reason: #312 (ADR 0246): the Default profile five minutes after start with its window in sight, through just perf-app (e2e/perf/memory.perf.ts), the median of two runs on the reference machine on 2026-11-16, a debug build with chromedriver attached, started at a load average of 3.6 and 1.1 with the other sessions paused: 3,540.5 and 3,580.1 MB in 29 processes, 24 of them renderers (2,910 and 2,934 MB). A desk in sight keeps every window and overlay live, so #312's change leaves it as it was: main read 3,552.0 and 3,537.6 MB the same day. Fails past allowedRegression on the platform its baseline was recorded on.

compose.reason: #32 §3: composing 15 live surfaces at 1440p within 4 ms leaves 12 of a 60 Hz frame's 16.7 ms to the engine's paints and the shell. Gated on the p95 frame of cargo bench -p desk-compositor --bench compose (every window moved and every texture repainted each frame, so every frame is a full redraw; animate, compose and GPU done), on a GPU; a software adapter (lavapipe, WARP) reports it. p95Ms and medianMs are the reference machine's, kept for the trend.

composeStartup.reason: The compositor's own start, which every desk start waits for before it shows anything: from asking for a GPU device to the first composed frame of the compose budget's desk with the GPU done (device, pipelines, the machine's fonts, 15 textures uploaded, the first glyphs). The same bench run's median of three starts after one that warms what the OS and the driver keep for a new binary (a fresh build's first start took 4 times as long). Fails past the allowance on the platform its baseline was recorded on; the desk's whole start is surfaceStartup's.

surfaceStartup.reason: The desk's start to the first composed frame holding a web surface's paint, the median of ten starts in a row after one that takes the OS's first look at a newly laid out bundle (3.6 s against 0.2 s); the slowest of the ten is judged against the same baseline and allowance, so one stalled start fails, and is kept beside it (slowestMs). Until #112 two starts in five spent 1.4 s more before the desk's main ran, busy machine or quiet: Chromium's code-sign clone hard-linked the executable at every start, so macOS's exec policy took it for a new binary and scanned it again; the shell turns the clone off, and #58 had taken the fastest of five. Starts whose CEF took over a second are counted in stalls. The CEF desk in compositor mode through its surface probe (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs), started by the test, so the process's start, CEF's, a renderer's, the page's first paint, its import and a compose all count. #35 measured 137 to 248 ms from CreateBrowser to the first paint alone. Fails past the allowance on the platform its baseline was recorded on.

surfaceMemory.page: the PoC's light page, animating, 800x600 at scale 2, composed at 1920x1080
surfaceMemory.source: #35 (spikes/compositor/README.md): 916 MiB for the whole process tree with 1 light surface, 2,002 MiB with 10, so (2,002 - 916) / 9 a surface
surfaceMemory.reason: What one more live surface costs the machine, the number the live budget (ADR 0142: visible windows and the 8 most recent) is set from: the process tree's physical footprint with 1 and with 10 animating light surfaces, the difference per surface, as #35 measured it (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs). Within 20 % of #35's either way: above means a surface costs more than the live budget assumed; below means the baseline is stale or the surfaces did not render. RSS on Linux and Windows is reported until #61 records their baselines. Since #111 (ADR 0152) every surface renders on the desk's frame clock (external begin frames): 121.1 to 130 MiB a surface on the reference machine, where #52's internal begin frames read 162 to 191 (179.5 on main the same day), the GPU process holding about 60 MiB a surface more; on Chromium's full pipeline (#117, ADR 0157) 117.5 to 119.7. #35's baseline stays: this is the number the live budget was set from.

inputToPaint.reason: #268 (ADR 0231): RT-16's 16 ms again, Chromium's full pipeline still off. What a press waited for was a begin frame sent before it: its surface had heard input within the second and took every desk frame, the display holds a begin frame a page has nothing to draw for to its deadline, a desk frame on, and CEF sends none meanwhile, so the press's prompts were not sent and it painted about 4 ms after what was left of that hold, 4 to 21 ms after the press; and as each paint came a fixed time after the web host's desk frame, a run's composed frames kept one phase against the probe desk's own 60 Hz. Input now brings a surface the next desk frame, the two after a paint and the slow frames (ten a second, counted from the last input), the paint a press waited for no longer counts as painting, and a page that changes for a press asks at once, which is the press's first prompt (web_host/frames_pacing.rs, frame_asks.js). Each of the probe's presses comes a twentieth of a desk frame later in the probe desk's frame than the one before, and within 200 ms of it: before the second slow frame, whose begin frame a press later than that finds out one time in six and waits up to a frame for (9 of 160 presses over 16 ms with the last four presses 190 to 210 ms apart; the gate does not see it). The probe alone on main b30d0628, twelve runs at a load average of 6.2 to 14.4 with main's build between them: the paint's p95 3.8 to 8.7 ms (main 15.7 to 23.0), its median 3.1 to 6.0 (5.2 to 12.6), the composed frame's median 12.5 to 16.2 (14.1 to 27.6; it is the paint's median plus the wait for the desk's next frame and its compose, 16.16 once with the paint's median at 5.96), a caught press's wait 0.0 to 0.02 (0.0 to 8.3). In three runs of just perf-compositor at a load average of 5.1 to 6.8, on a quieter machine whose cores wake later: the paint's p95 9.58, 10.40 and 15.98, its median 4.7 to 5.6, the composed frame's median 14.2 to 15.3, a caught press's wait 0.01; the values are the median run. budgetMs and caughtWaitBudgetMs are back at 16 and 2, where ADR 0210 had them at 22.5 and 8. Before, from #248 to #268: #248 (ADR 0210): Chromium's full pipeline is off, so a press paints later than RT-16's 16 ms, its target still (#268, under #249); the budgets hold what was measured on a quiet machine, with a margin. Without the full pipeline a begin frame the display gets before the page has handled the press is held to its deadline, a desk frame on, and CEF sends none meanwhile: a press's prompts start 2 ms after it (frames.rs PROMPT_AFTER), and the pressed surface takes no desk frame before them. Eleven runs on main 858309f2 at a load average under 6 at their start, five of just perf-compositor (the values are their median run) and six of the press probes alone: the paint's p95 15.6 to 20.4 ms, its median 6.6 to 12.6. budgetMs is the slowest plus 10 %, rounded up to the half millisecond: 22.5 (20.4); eighteen runs on main 9eabfa87 read 15.1 to 20.9, within it. The composed frame's median keeps RT-16's 16 ms (frameBudgetMs) and fails in some runs: without the full pipeline a run reads about 13 to 17 ms or about 24 to 27, a few between, on every commit measured (15.7 to 27.2 here; with the full pipeline 13.2 to 17.6 in eleven runs), as each press's composed frame comes a nearly constant time after its paint for the whole run (2 to 6 ms in one, 14 to 16 in another): the probe's presses keep their phase against the desk's 60 Hz frames from the run's start, and in a late run a paint just misses the frame that would show it. What decides that phase is #268's first target. The caught presses' wait after the busy-wait (ADR 0159) read 0.38 to 7.26 ms (0.01 to 6.86 on 9eabfa87): each caught press paints 10 to 20 ms after it on a quiet machine, so its paint lands in the busy-wait's 10 ms or up to 7 ms after it, and a run's median of five moves with that; caughtWaitBudgetMs is the slowest plus 10 %: 8. With the full pipeline the paint's p95 read 6.6 to 10.7 ms in eleven quiet runs (eight of main before this change, three between these). Before, from #117 to #248: RT-16, input to screen within 16 ms, on the compositor's input path (#56): a press sent to a surface as the router sends it (pointer.down and pointer.up), twenty times beside two animating surfaces, through the surface probe (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs). Two gates: the press to the surface's next paint reaching the compositor, p95 (p95Ms, what the engine and the import cost), and to the desk's first composed frame holding it, median (frameP50Ms). The frame waits for the desk's own 60 Hz clock, so its p95 is the paint's plus up to a frame, 19 to 24 ms here, and is kept for the trend (frameP95Ms) rather than gated; RT-16's 16 ms at p95 would need a compose on damage, not on the clock. Since #111 (ADR 0152) a surface renders only on the desk's begin frames, and each step of a paint (the renderer's frame, the display's draw, the capture) waits for one: a press on an idle surface brings begin frames every 1 ms from the press until its paint. Since #117 (ADR 0157) Chromium runs its full pipeline, so a begin frame an idle page had nothing to draw for no longer holds the next ones back for a whole frame (CEF sends none while one is out), the one press in ten #111 saw wait a frame. The values are #117's median run of five at a load average of 5 to 8: the paint's p95 read 4.9 to 9.2 ms and the frame's median 13.5 to 14.7, where main read 9.4 to 14.2 and 15.2 to 15.8 in three runs the same hour (#111 read 12.1 to 22.3 and 13.9 to 17.9 on a busier machine). Since #129 (ADR 0159) five more presses are caught on purpose by CEF's busy-wait (a task delayed 5 ms after the press and CEF's work run at once, so that call loops out its 10 ms slice, as Chromium's own timers make one do now and then): gated, their paint's wait after the busy-wait ends, the median (caughtWaitMs within caughtWaitBudgetMs), since the frame clock's begin frames go out from a stand-in thread meanwhile and CEF's busy-wait runs them; kept for the trend, the press to that paint (caughtPaintP50Ms, at least the slice's 10 ms, as the desk's event loop waits for the call). #129's five runs at a load average of 8 to 13: the wait 0.01 to 0.04 ms (0.92 in a sixth run), the press to the paint 10.7 to 11.4; main's pump read 4.1 to 5.0 ms and 13.7 to 16.4 in the probe. The twenty presses read 5.3 to 12.2 ms at p95 (two of them caught by chance in the 12.2) and 13.0 to 15.5 at the frame's median.

inputFromRest.reason: #268 (ADR 0231): the budget stays ADR 0210's, and what a press at rest waits for is the GPU, not a begin frame. In Chromium's trace of the probe no begin frame was missed: the page had handled the press by 0.5 to 1.9 ms, the display drew its frame 3.2 to 4.3 ms after the press, and the capture's copy ended 8 to 18 ms after it, as the GPU woke (ADR 0162): the desk's own wake-up copy finished 2.9 to 14.8 ms after the press in 37 presses, and the paint 1.9 to 7.2 ms after that. The 21 to 25 ms a block reads is the probe's own: its desk composes a frame 16.7 ms after a press at rest, that compose waits 8 to 9 ms for the cold GPU with CEF's work behind it, and a paint due after 16.7 ms comes at about 25. Turn by turn on main b30d0628: main read 8.6 to 26.2 ms at p95 in nine runs at a load average of 3.0 to 11.3 (over 16 in six), ADR 0231's build 6.6 to 20.6 in five at 3.1 to 14.0 (over 16 in two), and 17.3, 24.2 and 25.3 in three runs of just perf-compositor at 5.1 to 6.8; a quiet machine wakes later (main 23.3 ms at the median at a load average of 3.0). 16 ms at p95 needs the GPU awake at the press, or a capture without the copy; the values are still ADR 0210's median run. Before, from #248 to #268: #248 (ADR 0210): Chromium's full pipeline is off, so a press on a desk at rest paints later than RT-16's 16 ms, its target still (#268, under #249). The desk's clock looks at a press at once, and on a desk at rest that look is a desk frame: its begin frame went out with the press, before the page had handled it, the display held it to its deadline, and the press paid a frame (34.8 to 35.4 ms at p95 in fifteen runs on a quiet machine). The pressed surface now takes no desk frame before its first prompt, 2 ms after the press (frames.rs). Eleven runs on main 858309f2 at a load average under 6 at their start, five of just perf-compositor (the values are their median run) and six of the probe alone: 13.1 to 24.3 ms at p95. A block of twelve presses reads about 13 to 17 ms or about 21 to 25 (14 of 33 blocks; a page at rest that misses a press's first begin frame paints about 25 ms after the press, and a later first prompt made that more often), so a run's median block read 20.5 or more in three of the eleven. budgetMs is the slowest plus 10 %, rounded up to the half millisecond: 27 (24.3); thirteen runs on main 9eabfa87 read 21.3 to 25.9, within it. With the full pipeline 13.6 to 16.3 in three runs between these (its nine blocks 13.1 to 18.4), and 21.7 to 24.7 in eight quieter runs of main before this change. Before, from #133 to #248: #133 (ADR 0162): RT-16 on a desk at rest, through the surface probe's idle-input run (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs): three still surfaces, two of them the click page, pressed in turn twelve times, each press after the desk rested 2, 2.5 or 3 s (the probe's loop run as the window's at rest), so every pressed surface is long idle on the slow clock (ADR 0157) and nothing on the desk has painted for seconds. Gated: the press to its paint reaching the compositor, p95 (the second slowest of twelve), within budgetMs. Kept for the trend: the median, the slowest, and the composed frame's median, which waits for the desk's next frame (16.7 ms after the press: the desk composed nothing at rest). After a second or more with nothing painted the GPU sleeps, and the first copy after (Chromium's capture in its GPU process, the desk's attach in its own) took 3 to 12 ms to finish where a busy desk's takes a fraction of one; neither the slow clock, the renderer nor CEF's pump was the wait. Main painted 10.0 to 16.9 ms after the press at the median and 10.2 to 23.3 at p95 in six runs at a load average of 2.5 to 6, over the budget in four; with input to a cold desk waking the GPU's copies at once (apps/desk/shell/src/web_host/copy_wake.rs) 8.3 to 14.7 and 12.9 to 16.1 in nine runs, within it in eight (16.07 once, at a load average of 2.5). Its floor is the GPU's own wake-up, which starts at the press: a copy of a few pixels took 4 to 13 ms to finish on a quiet machine. #148: the machine's cores set the rest of the floor. The gate read 8.0 to 8.4 ms in #134's runs and 15.1 to 21.6 later the same day; run by run, presses painted 5.8 to 15.8 ms after them on a quiet machine and 6.5 to 7.8 with one busy loop anywhere on it, and a core kept busy by the desk from the press on did not help. So the run presses once first, not counted, then three blocks of twelve (blocks, warmUp), and the gate reads the block whose p95 is the median (blockP95Ms keeps all three): a burst of other work during one block, or its end, does not decide a run. Five runs at a load average of 3.9 to 7.3: 12.69 to 13.21 ms (blocks 12.41 to 14.92). The values are the median run of the five; tries counts the median block's presses.

deskAtRest.reason: #129 (ADR 0159), #134 (ADR 0164): what a desk at rest costs, through the surface probe's rest run (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs): three still surfaces, shown and awake, each long idle, which since #134 take no begin frames, and the probe's loop run for ten seconds as the compositor window's event loop runs (a turn, then a wait for CEF's next work, the clock's next look or CEF's ask). Gated: the loop's wake-ups a second (each turn of the event loop) within wakeupsBudget, where main's pump woke 54.6 to 57.7 times (its poll every 33 ms whatever the clock did), #129's 33.2 to 38.3 (CEF's answers to the slow clock's ten begin frames a second a surface) and #134's 10.1 to 10.3 (CEF's poll every 100 ms, ADR 0159); the browser process's CPU within cpuBudgetPercent of a core (0.5 to 0.7 %); and after the rest a fourth page that changes itself by a timer, three times, each once it is long idle: from each change to its paint, the median within ownChangeBudgetMs (49.6 to 51.6 ms: its page asks for frames, frame_asks.js; the slow clock read 107; since ADR 0231 a page whose frames have stopped asks at its change, not 40 ms on: 9.6, 11.2 and 17.8 ms in three runs at a load average of 5.1 to 6.8, and ownChangeMs and ownChangeMaxMs are their median run's). Kept for the trend: the browser process's OS wake-ups (macOS proc_pid_rusage: 30.6 to 30.7 a second, CEF's own threads), CEF's work calls a second, the begin frames a second (none) and the slowest own change; a press from rest is inputFromRest's since #133. The values are #134's median run of five at a load average of 5 to 8.

freshDeskAtRest.reason: #134 (ADR 0164): a fresh desk left alone, through just perf-app (e2e/perf/rest.perf.ts): the Default profile with its first run, gone through as a person in a hurry does (Skip for now, Later, Not now, a name, the first suggested task), then twenty seconds alone and ten measured with ps: the app's own process's CPU as a share of one core, within budgetPercent, a budget that fails from the first run (no baseline needed), and its whole tree's kept beside it. Before #134 it read 59.2 % (its tree 124.9 %): the first run's animation, Eris's idle motion drawn on a canvas at every frame in the shell page and in her floating window, the runtime's ticker and the page's report asking for a frame at every frame, messages waking every surface for a second, and on the reference machine's locked screen the compositor composing at every desk frame for a window that withheld its frames. After: 3.1 to 3.4 % in three runs at a load average of 5 to 9 (its tree 5.3 to 5.7 %). On 2026-11-11 the same head read 6.6 to 6.8 % at a load average of 4 to 5: the palette, never summoned, took Chromium's 60 Hz begin frames in its page and its frame, the desk's own process answering each. Since #147 a hidden floating window's page is hidden (apps/desk/shell/src/pane.rs): 2.8, 2.8, 3.0 and 3.2 % in four runs in a row at a load average of 3.8 to 5.5 (its tree 3.8 to 4.8 %), against 3.6 and 6.1 % (5.9 and 11.6 %) without it the same hour. Left: on the e2e desk Eris floats (the desk is not the app in front) and her window takes Chromium's 60 Hz begin frames with an idle page; CEF's busy-wait (ADR 0159) about twice a second for a delayed task of Chromium's own; endue.docker's proc.spawn every few seconds. The values are the median run of the four (#147's).

deskOutOfSight.reason: #155: a desk nobody can see, through just perf-app (e2e/perf/hidden.perf.ts): the main window closed with its red button, then minimized, each ten seconds measured once three have passed (the spin started within about 3 s), then brought back as the Dock icon does it. Gated, each the worse of the two: the app's own process's CPU as a share of one core within budgetPercent, freshDeskAtRest's budget for a desk in sight; the event loop's turns a second (compositor_stats' pump.turns) within turnsBudget, under a visible desk's 24 to 78 at rest; and from the window brought back to its first composed frame within shownBudgetMs. All three are budgets, failing from the first run. Before #155 the main process spun at 99 to 100 % and 14,000 to 19,000 turns a second for as long as the window was out of sight, closed, minimized, hidden, covered or on another Space: the frame clock named a frame due at the last one's time, long past, and the loop never waited. Where the OS says nothing of a window out of sight (a locked screen; X11 without a window manager) the spec feeds the event winit hands the shell itself (compositor_window { occluded }) and keeps told: false beside the values: the wait it checks is the desk's own. On the reference machine with its screen locked (the OS said nothing, so the spec fed it), a debug build on a machine busy with other work: 1.3 to 1.4 % and 29 to 38 turns a second out of sight with the driver attached (16 to 22 without it), the frame 35 to 48 ms after the window came back; the same run on the old frame rule failed at 100.3 % and 42,581 turns a second.

residentAtRest.reason: #312 (ADR 0246): a desk nobody sees holds only the live budget's windows (ADR 0142), and its hidden overlays sleep, so its tree's RSS is a third lower. Three runs on the reference machine on 2026-11-16, a debug build with chromedriver attached, each started at a load average under 4 (3.8 to 4.0) with the other sessions paused: 2,270.8, 2,258.5 and 2,270.2 MB in 19 processes, 14 of them renderers (1,697 to 1,709 MB), where main read 3,445, 3,425 and 3,426 MB in 29 processes with 24 renderers the same day (load 1.0 to 3.1); two runs started at a load of 13 and 7.8 read 2,302 and 2,273 and are not counted. Of the Default profile's fourteen plugin windows the eight most recent stay live (desk.surfaces.live) and the one with the keys beside them; the launcher, the palette, permissions, universal and views, never shown, sleep until the window comes back or they are summoned. The memory follows the renderers: each holds about 116 MB of RSS (35 MB of physical footprint; RSS counts the framework pages each helper maps again); the browser holds 286, the GPU process 134, the network and storage services 77 and 61; the spec keeps the kinds beside the sum (kinds). rssBudgetMb is 2,500 MB, the largest counted reading and a tenth more (2,270.8 × 1.1, rounded up): a desk that keeps one renderer more than now stays within it, and two more fail it. rssMb is the median run. The CPU readings stay #237's: 1.0 to 1.1 % for the app's own process and 2.6 to 3.1 % for its tree in these runs. Before, from #237 to #312: #237 (ADR 0225): endue at rest with no window, through just perf-app (e2e/perf/resident.perf.ts): the Default profile without the first run, its main window closed with its red button (the desk runs on and the island shows over other apps), twenty seconds alone and thirty measured with ps: the app's own process's CPU as a share of one core, its whole tree's, and the tree's summed RSS at the end. All three are budgets, failing from the first run. Four runs on the reference machine on 2026-11-15, a debug build with chromedriver attached, while other work ran on it (load average 5 to 28): the app's own process 0.5, 0.5, 0.8 and 1.1 %, its tree 1.9, 2.2, 3.4 and 3.6 %, the tree's RSS 3,547 to 3,585 MB in 29 processes (idleMemory, the window in sight, read 3,603 MB the same hour). targetPercent is #237's figure, under 1 % of a core: three runs of four were under it and one was not, so the gate is budgetPercent, 2 %, about twice the slowest reading, until a quiet runner has read it; treeBudgetPercent is 6 %, the slowest reading and two thirds more; rssBudgetMb is 4,000 MB, the largest reading and about a tenth more. The memory is the Default profile's thirteen plugin windows with their pages still live fifty seconds after the window closed: the live budget (ADR 0142) puts a page out of sight to sleep after desk.display.unload-after (300 s), which this run does not wait for. Hidden pages keep their timers' pace (ADR 0225), so a plugin that polls costs here what it costs in sight. The values are the full run's (the first of the four).
